author: General Practitioner
note_text:
61F w/ several months hx intermittent L-sided headache. Localized to L temporal/mandibular region. Described as dull, occasionally sharp, lasting hrs–days. No N/V, no aura, no visual symptoms. No trauma.
Exam:
- neuro non-focal
- CN intact
- no palpable masses
Assessment: likely tension-type HA vs early neuropathic pain.
Plan: trial NSAIDs, monitor progression.

author: Neurologist
note_text:
Progression of symptoms over past months. ↑ frequency + intensity. Pain now more localized to L jaw region, occasionally triggered by chewing.
Exam:
- mild tenderness L mandibular region
- no trigeminal sensory deficit
- no facial weakness
Assessment: atypical facial pain vs trigeminal neuralgia (atypical).
Plan: start neuropathic pain agent. MRI head/neck ordered.

author: Radiologist
note_text:
Multiple nodular lesions along course of L masseteric nerve.
Extension into:
- pterygopalatine fossa
- parapharyngeal space
Morphology: "string-of-beads" appearance.
Impression: multifocal peripheral nerve sheath tumor → most consistent w/ schwannoma.

author: Neurology / Head & Neck Surgery / Radiology Team
note_text: Imaging reviewed. Multifocal lesions consistent w/ benign schwannomas. Clinical correlation: lesion likely symptomatic source of pain. Plan: recommend surgical excision for symptom relief + histological confirmation.

author: Head & Neck Surgeon
note_text:
61F w/ symptomatic multifocal masseteric nerve schwannoma. Discussed risks:
- nerve injury
- facial weakness
- incomplete excision
Given symptoms + tumor extent → surgical excision indicated. Pt understands + agrees to proceed.

author: Surgical Team
note_text: Pt admitted for planned excision. No interval change in symptoms. Vitals stable. Pain present but controlled. Assessment: fit for surgery. Plan: proceed to OR.

author: Head & Neck Surgeon
note_text:
Exploration performed. Multiple interconnected nodular tumors identified along masseteric nerve, extending into adjacent spaces. "String-of-beads" configuration confirmed intraoperatively. Careful dissection performed w/ preservation of surrounding structures. Nodules excised sequentially. Outcome:
- complete gross excision achieved
- no intraop complications

author: Surgeon
note_text:
Stable postop. Exam:
- no facial nerve deficit
- pain significantly improved vs pre-op
Plan: continue routine postop care.

author: Ward Nurse
note_text: Pt comfortable. Pain controlled w/ oral analgesia. Vitals stable. No new neuro deficit. Tolerating oral intake.

author: Pathologist
note_text: Specimen: multiple nodular masses from L masseteric region. Histology: encapsulated benign tumor, spindle cell pattern consistent w/ schwannoma. Conclusion: benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor.

author: Surgeon
note_text: Continues to improve. Pain minimal. No neurological deficit. Wound clean. Plan: discharge planning.

author: Surgeon
note_text: Postop course uncomplicated following complete excision of multifocal schwannoma. Pain resolved. No deficits. Discharge: stable, ambulatory. Plan: outpatient follow-up.

author: Surgeon
note_text:
Pt reports marked improvement. No recurrence of head pain. Exam:
- wound healing well
- no neuro deficit
Assessment: good early surgical outcome.

author: Neurologist
note_text: Pt asymptomatic. No residual facial pain. Assessment: complete resolution of hemicrania post tumor removal.

author: Surgeon
note_text: No recurrence of symptoms. Functional status normal. Plan: routine surveillance.
